SYSTEM INSTRUCTION — SECTOR POST-SESSION REVIEW

Same spirit as general post-market autopsy, but the object is ONE sector ETF and its
environment — not SPX.

INPUTS (injected):
1. Morning sector prediction for this sector
2. Channel 1: actual sector ETF open/close/% change; SPY % change; relative return
3. Archived morning ETF context

STEPS (do not skip):
0. FACTS: sector ETF %, SPY %, relative %, path if known
1. What drove the sector today (taxonomy-aligned factors preferred)
2. Audit morning S0–S4 reads against reality (use morning numbers, not post-close
   rewrites of the morning)
3. Interactions / double-count / knowable-at-open test
4. Outliers inside the sector

Evidence: CLAIM/URL/PUBLISHED/QUOTE/SUMMARY format for factual claims.

SECTOR: <name>
ETF: <ticker>
ETF_PCT: <number>

Produce the required output exactly as specified above, then append a final section titled RESEARCH APPENDIX listing the queries you ran, the key sources (title + URL + timestamp where available), and the specific facts you took from each. Never invent sources.

Last graded **2026-10-08 down/mild vs XLB +0.592% (dir MISS)** — the recurring failure is signing down on stale levels while the live tape/PM resolves up. Scope DO-INSTEAD: **cut conviction when sign fights sector tape; prefer flat/mild on conflict** (10-02, 10-08 losses). Active XLB rules checked: **Hormuz/oil-risk-off override lesson (9-14-style) is ON** — do not pay a commodity floor when the commodity complex IS the shock source; expect metals to co-move with equities. **a-materials-call macro-overlay cap is partially ON** — prior SPY slightly red, Hormuz/oil headlines live, but **no same-morning China hard-data miss today** (China Sept PMI was an expansion print, Oct 1), so the hard flat-cap does not fully bind. **10-02 unprinted-binary rule OFF** (no fresh binary pre-open; FOMC minutes already printed hawkish; CPI later this week is a level, not a same-morning print). **8/25 / 8/27 S4 conviction caps ON** (1d rel +0.08%, not confirmed-up).

## Analysis — XLB, session of 2026-10-13 (Tuesday cash)

This is a **Hormuz/kinetic-oil risk-off morning colliding with a green XLB premarket print (+0.76%)** — the single most important tension on the card. Asia is sharply red (Kospi −5.46%, Nikkei −1.82%, composite −1.37%), NQ premarket −0.73% vs ES only −0.09% — a tech-led risk-off, not a broad liquidation. Europe is mildly green. XLB is the #2 PM on the sector board behind XLP, with XLE/XLF/XLRE all green — a defensive/commodity-adjacent rotation, not cyclical beta.

**Spine check (S1):** Copper is **firm as a level** (COMEX +0.66%, LME ~$14.7k/t) but ~4% below the Sep-10 record — no squeeze continuation. Iron ore −0.14%, HRC −0.16%, Newcastle coal −1.53%, lumber −1.32% — industrial complex soft. **Gold took a −$100 flush on hawkish Fed comments** (AEM down; though Finviz GC shows +0.46/0.90% on the 1d futures frame — treat the flush as the live increment per News Judge #4, the 8/14 sleeve is now a headwind, not a book bid). MAP HEAT is majority-down (Ag inputs, Aluminum, Building materials, Coking coal, Copper, Gold, Other industrial metals, Precious — all down, low conviction; Chemicals flat). China Sept PMI expansion (50.1, first since June) is a **level positive**, not a fresh same-morning catalyst.

**Macro overlay (S0):** Hawkish FOMC minutes ("another hike likely"), 10Y ~5.22% elevated, real yields +0.41 on the month, and a fresh Hormuz/Iran/Houthi oil escalation (WTI ~$104 level, offered today but the *situation* is live). On oil/geopolitical risk-off days, metals correlate toward equities — the commodity bid is NOT a floor. USD +2.8% on the month is a month-level headwind.

**Tape (S4):** XLB PM **+0.76% green vs flat ES** is real confirmation of relative bid — but per 8/25/8/27 it caps at +0.5 max, and the sign fights my factor sum, so confidence must shrink per the DO-INSTEAD.

Resolution: leading factors (S0–S3) net ~−2, S4 mildly positive → **down/mild, low confidence**, regime risk_off. The Kospi/NQ red Asia open plus hawkish-rates + oil-escalation regime outweighs a defensive-rotation PM print; but the XLB PM green and the persistent post-PMI China level forbid anything stronger than mild.

## 0. Facts

XLB **+0.566%**, SPY **−0.012%**, relative **+0.578%**. Open **49.70** → close **49.72** (high ~49.92, low ~49.35). Path: gap/hold vs prior close (~49.44), not an open-to-close melt-up; cash barely moved vs the open, but the **prior-close return stayed green** and beat a flat SPY. Actual: **up / mild**. Morning call: **down / mild** (score −1.893, conf 0.35–0.48, divergence flagged). **Direction miss, magnitude hit.**

This is the same failure the card already named: signing down on stale macro/HEAT while live PM/tape was green (10-02, 10-08).

## 1. What drove the sector

Not a materials-demand boom and not a Hormuz metals dump. Cash was a **chemicals/coatings carry** inside a **narrow, tech/healthcare risk-off** tape:

- Energy led (~XLE **+1.8%**); materials a weaker commodity-adjacent cousin (**+0.57%**).
- **LIN +0.98%**, **SHW +1.22%**, **APD +1.79%** lifted the cap-weighted ETF (LIN ~13% of XLB).
- **FCX −1.19%**, **NEM −1.33%** as COMEX copper settled **−0.31%** to **$6.6780** and gold eased.
- SPY flat on mixed bank earnings, JNJ ~−6%, China DRAM/chip scare (MU −3.62%) — **tech-led, not broad liquidation**.
- Hormuz stayed live; WTI **$94.14 (+0.43%)**, Brent **$105.69 (−0.9%)**. That bid **energy**, it did not force XLB down.

Taxonomy: **sector rotation into commodity-adjacent / chemicals** + **risk-off that stayed in XLK/XLV/XLF**, not industrial-metal surge, not gold surge, not China demand shock.

## 2. Morning S0–S4 vs reality

Use **morning numbers**, not a rewrite.

| Sleeve | Morning | Reality | Audit |
|---|---|---|---|
| **S0 −1** hawkish minutes, 10Y ~5.22%, Hormuz risk-off, “metals co-move with equities” | 10Y **5.24%**; Hormuz live; gold softer | **Half-right on rates/gold, wrong on the overlay.** Risk-off was chips/JNJ, not materials. Hormuz funded **XLE**, not an XLB liquidation. |
| **S1 −1** Cu +0.66% “level not squeeze”; ore/steel/coal soft; gold −$100 flush; HEAT majority-down | Cu **reversed to −0.31%**; gold down; miners down | **Right on metals, wrong on the ETF.** XLB is chemicals-heavy; LIN/SHW/APD offset miner drag. |
| **S2 −1** breadth failure | Miners red, chemicals green, ETF green | **Directionally useful as mixed internals**, too harsh as a −1 that helped flip the sign. Morning’s own “ETF up / heat down” PARTIAL was the better read. |
| **S3 0** no flows | Still no clean flow print | **Fine.** |
| **S4 +0.5** XLB PM **+0.76%** vs ES **−0.09%** | Cash **+0.57%** vs SPY **−0.01%**, rel **+0.58%**; open≈close | **The sleeve that was right.** PM relative bid **held**. Skill multiplier **S4 = 0.0** zeroed the only confirming tape. |

HIT grid: Risk-off tape HIT was **overfit** (Asia/NQ red ≠ XLB red). Sector rotation PARTIAL and breadth-failure PARTIAL were the hits that should have **blocked a down sign**. Gold surge MISS was confirmed. Industrial-metal surge PARTIAL overstated Cu, which faded in cash.

## 3. Interactions / double-count / knowable-at-open

**Double-count:** Hormuz entered as (a) S0 risk-off, (b) 9-14 “don’t pay a commodity floor,” and (c) index_carry **−1.692** / general **−6.767** / llm_overlay **−3.825**. Same oil shock was counted three times as **bearish XLB**. In cash it was **bullish XLE** and **mildly bullish chemicals-XLB**.

**Sign vs tape:** Leading sum **−2.5** vs S4/PM **+0.5**. Divergence **True**. DO-INSTEAD said **prefer flat/mild on conflict**. Pipeline still printed **down**. Calendar size-gate kept **mild** (correct) but did not flip sign to **flat**.

**Knowable at open:** PM green, ES flat, XLE/XLP/XLRE green vs XLK, divergence flag, 8/25–8/27 cap, 10-08 miss pattern. **Not knowable:** Cu PM +0.66% → settle −0.31%; LIN/SHW/APD vs FCX/NEM split; JNJ/bank/DRAM keeping SPY unchanged instead of cascade.

**KNOWABLE_AT_OPEN: partially.** The instruction to **not sign down** was knowable; the chemicals-vs-miners mix was not.

## 4. Outliers inside the sector

- **APD +1.79% / SHW +1.22% / LIN +0.98%** vs **NEM −1.33% / FCX −1.19%** — ETF ≠ copper tape.
- **XLE ≫ XLB**: Hormuz paid energy, not miners.
- Gold/miners followed the hawkish-rates sleeve; **they were not the XLB residual.**
